qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by the Delaware Division of Public Health for health programs and services, with detailed submission instructions, deadlines, evaluation criteria, and contract terms.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
This request for proposals (“RFP”) is issued pursuant to 29 Del. C. §§ 6981 and 6982.
Date: September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT
Eligibility:  This RFP is open to private organizations.
All proposals must be submitted prior to 1:00 PM EDT on September 15, 2026.

findings.title: Conflicting Contract Start Dates
findings.fact: Page 2 states the estimated project start date is July 1, 2027, but page 4 states contracts for funded awards are anticipated to begin July 1, 2028. Page 17 confirms the contract term is anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028.
findings.business_implication: Bidders cannot plan resources, staffing, or pricing reliably due to a one-year discrepancy in the anticipated start date.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from the State through the Q&A process regarding the correct contract start date.

quotes.quote: Estimated Project Start Date       Date: July 1, 2027
No contract or grant agreement will be executed, and no funds will be paid, unless and until such appropriation is enacted; contracts for funded awards are anticipated to begin July 1, 2028.
Contract term is one (1) year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation.

findings.title: Detailed Scope of Work Not Provided
findings.fact: The RFP references Appendix B for scope of work and technical requirements, but Appendix B appears blank in the provided document.
findings.business_implication: Bidders cannot confidently prepare a proposal or price the services without understanding the detailed requirements.
findings.action_recommendation: Request the full Appendix B from the procurement contact and verify whether additional appendices were omitted from the RFP package.

quotes.quote: Please refer to Appendix B -for details/requirements for the Scope of Service.

APPENDIX B 
SCOPE OF WORK AND TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

findings.title: Eligibility Limited to Private Organizations
findings.fact: The RFP states it is open only to private organizations; state-operated programs must not respond.
findings.business_implication: Public entities and state-operated programs are ineligible to bid and may waste effort if they respond.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that your organization qualifies as a private organization under 16 Del. C. § 137(i) before investing in a proposal.

quotes.quote: Eligibility:  This RFP is open to private organizations.  State-operated programs do not respond to this RFP; funding for state-operated programs is designated by the Department through a separate internal process pursuant to 16 Del. C. § 137(i)(1).

findings.title: Broad General Indemnification with No Cap
findings.fact: The vendor agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the State from any and all liability, suits, actions, or claims arising out of the vendor's performance, including attorney's fees.
findings.business_implication: The vendor faces potentially unlimited financial exposure for any claims related to contract performance, regardless of fault apportionment.
findings.action_recommendation: Evaluate the availability of insurance coverage and consult legal counsel; consider proposing a mutual indemnification clause or a damages cap in Attachment 4 exceptions.

quotes.quote: By submitting a proposal, the proposing vendor agrees that in the event it is awarded a contract, it will indemnify and otherwise hold harmless the State of Delaware, its agents and employees from any and all liability, suits, actions, or claims, together with all costs, expenses for attorney’s fees, arising out of the vendor’s, its agents and employees’ performance work or services in connection with the contract.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Proposals must be submitted electronically before 1:00 PM EDT on September 15, 2026, via Euna Procurement (formerly Bonfire).
findings.business_implication: Late submissions are rejected; the online portal may have upload delays, so bidders should plan to upload well in advance.
findings.action_recommendation: Create a timeline to complete all required forms and upload the proposal at least 24 hours before the deadline to avoid technical issues.

quotes.quote: All proposals must be submitted prior to 1:00 PM EDT on September 15, 2026.
To be considered, all proposals must be submitted in through Euna Procurement (formerly Bonfire) at    https://dhss.bonfirehub.com/ and respond to the items outlined in this RFP.

findings.title: Evaluation Criteria Weights
findings.fact: Proposals are scored on Statement of Need (15), Alignment with Health Fund Priorities (25), Program Design and Feasibility (20), Measurable Outcomes (20), Organizational Capacity (10), and Budget Reasonableness (10), totaling 100 points.
findings.business_implication: Bidders should allocate proposal effort to align with the highest-weighted criteria, particularly Health Fund priorities (tobacco/cancer).
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the proposal explicitly demonstrates alignment with tobacco prevention/cessation and cancer prevention/detection/treatment to maximize scoring.

quotes.quote: Statement of Need (§ II.A of proposal)-Delaware-specific evidence of the health need and the service gap the program fills; for returning organizations, including prior-year results. [15] Alignment with Health Fund Priorities (§ II.B)-fit with the purposes in 16 Del. C. § 137(d), with the strongest weight for direct ties to tobacco prevention and cessation and to cancer prevention, detection, and treatment. [25] Program Design and Feasibility (§ II.C)-goals, activities, timeline, staffing, and geographic reach that are specific, coherent, and achievable within the contract year. [20] Measurable Outcomes and Evaluation Plan (§ II.D)-specific, verifiable objectives with indicators, targets, and data sources, suitable for incorporation into the award agreement. [20] Organizational Capacity & Past Performance (§ II.E)-governance, financial management, audit history, and experience operating programs of similar scope. [10] Budget Reasonableness and Sustainability (§ II.F)= justified costs proportionate to reach, documented other funding, and a realistic plan given declining Master Settlement Agreement revenue. [10] Total 100

findings.title: No Advance Payments and Possible 25% Holdback
findings.fact: Payments are made based on defined milestones, not in advance, and the State may hold back up to 25% of contract monies until acceptable performance is demonstrated.
findings.business_implication: Bidders need adequate cash flow to fund operations since payment may be delayed and a significant portion may be withheld.
findings.action_recommendation: Incorporate milestone-based invoicing and cash flow projections into the budget; negotiate acceptable holdback terms during contract negotiations.

quotes.quote: Payments for services will not be made in advance of work performed.    The State of Delaware may require holdback of contract monies until acceptable performance is demonstrated (as much as 25%).

findings.title: Prohibition on Offshore Work
findings.fact: All work must be performed within the United States; no activity may be executed in an offshore facility, and the vendor must attest to this in the transmittal letter.
findings.business_implication: Vendors with international operations or subcontractors may be disqualified or forced to reallocate resources.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct an internal review of all proposed delivery locations and ensure the transmittal letter contains the required attestation.

quotes.quote: No activity is to be executed in an offshore facility, either by a subcontracted firm or a foreign office or division of the vendor.  The vendor must attest to the fact that no activity will take place outside of the United States in its transmittal letter.  Failure to adhere to this requirement is cause for elimination from future consideration.

findings.title: Termination for Non-Appropriation
findings.fact: The contract terminates if the General Assembly fails to appropriate funds necessary for the agreement.
findings.business_implication: Even after award, the contract may be cancelled without liability if funding is not appropriated, creating financial uncertainty for the vendor.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for potential non-appropriation by including contingency clauses in subcontracts and maintaining flexibility in resource commitments.

quotes.quote: In the event the General Assembly fails to appropriate the specific funds necessary to enter into or continue the contractual agreement, in whole or part, the agreement shall be terminated as to any obligation of the State requiring the expenditure of money for which no specific appropriation is available at the end of the last fiscal year for which no appropriation is available or upon the exhaustion of funds.

findings.title: Mandatory Attachments and Forms
findings.fact: Proposals must include the transmittal letter, Vendor Information Form, Non-Collusion Statement, Exception Form, Confidentiality Form, Business References, and Workplan Template; Subcontractor Form is required if subcontractors are used.
findings.business_implication: Missing any mandatory attachment can render the proposal non-responsive and lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Use Appendix A as a compliance checklist and verify all required forms are completed, signed, and uploaded before the deadline.

quotes.quote: The items listed above provide the basis for evaluating each vendor’s proposal.  Failure to provide all appropriate information may deem the submitting vendor as “non-responsive” and exclude the vendor from further consideration.

One (1) completed Vendor information Sheet (See Attachment 2 – in Appendix C).  One (1) complete and signed Non-collusion agreement (See Attachment 3 – in Appendix C).  One (1) completed RFP Exception form (See Attachment 4 – in Appendix C) – please check box if no information – Form must be included.  One (1) completed Confidentiality Form (See Attachment 5 – in Appendix C) – please check if no information is deemed confidential – Form must be included.  One (1) completed Business Reference form (See Attachment 6 – in Appendix C)) – please provide references other than State of Delaware contacts – Form must be included.  One (1) complete and signed copy of the Subcontractor Information Form (See Attachment 7 – in Appendix C)) for each subcontractor – only provide if applicable.  Completed the Appendix E - Sample Workplan Template.

findings.title: Prices Fixed Through June 30, 2028
findings.fact: Prices quoted in the proposal must remain fixed and binding on the bidder at least through June 30, 2028.
findings.business_implication: Bidders must account for inflation and cost increases over a nearly two-year period without the ability to adjust pricing.
findings.action_recommendation: Factor known cost escalations into the proposed budget and consider including an escalation clause in the exception form if permitted.

quotes.quote: Prices quoted in the proposal shall remain fixed and binding on the bidder at least through June  30,  2028.

findings.title: Mandatory Monthly and Quarterly Reporting
findings.fact: Awarded vendors must submit a Monthly Usage Report (Attachment 8) by the 15th of each month, even if no spend occurred, and a quarterly Subcontracting 2nd Tier Report (Attachment 9).
findings.business_implication: Ongoing administrative burden and a potential default risk if reports are incomplete or late, which could lead to contract cancellation.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish a reporting calendar and assign responsibility for preparing and submitting these reports to ensure compliance.

quotes.quote: A complete and accurate Usage Report (Attachment 8) shall be furnished in an Excel format and submitted electronically, no later than the 15th (or next business day after the 15th day) of each month, detailing the purchasing of all items and/or services on this contract.

findings.title: Conflicting Advisory Committee and Award List Dates
findings.fact: Page 2 lists the Health Fund Advisory Committee Public Meeting on November 6, 2026 and Final Recommended Award List Transmitted on November 13, 2026, while page 4 states the public meeting is no later than November 7, 2026 and the final list is transmitted no later than November 15, 2026.
findings.business_implication: Bidders may be confused about the procurement timeline and when to expect award decisions.
findings.action_recommendation: Monitor the Q&A responses and addenda to confirm the official schedule; rely on the formal addendum over the initial RFP if discrepancies are corrected.

quotes.quote: Health Fund Advisory Committee Public Meeting          Date: November 6, 2026
Final Recommended Award List Transmitted:          Date: November 13, 2026

reviewed by the Health Fund Advisory Committee at a public meeting with public testimony no later than November 7, 2026, and transmitted as a final recommended award list to the Governor, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, the Controller General, and the members of the Joint Finance Committee no later than November 15, 2026.
